headline: Certificate transparency can be issued, not only verified.
summary: The toolkit verified SCTs but could not issue the certificates that carry them, so a CA running certificate transparency had to hand-encode both RFC 6962 extensions. pki.x509.sign now issues the precertificate a log is given and the certificate that embeds the SCTs it returns. A precertificate whose poison was supplied pre-encoded and non-critical was signed and validated as an ordinary certificate; that is now refused.

Added: extensions.precertificatePoison: true issues a precertificate (RFC 6962 section 3.1). The poison is emitted critical with an ASN.1 NULL value, which is what stops a standard X.509v3 client from accepting a precertificate as an issued certificate: pki.path.validate refuses one, where the same leaf without the poison validates.

extensions.signedCertificateTimestampList takes the SCTs a log returned, in the shape pki.ct.signSct and pki.ct.parseSctList already use, and embeds them in the certificate issued after the log answers (section 3.3, at least one). It is always emitted non-critical, since a client that does not recognize the OID refuses a certificate that marks it critical. A client recovers the signed entry from the issued certificate with pki.ct.x509CertEntry, and an SCT embedded this way verifies against that entry. A spec naming both the poison and an SCT list is refused, because they name opposite ends of one exchange and a certificate carrying both could never have its SCTs verified.
Fixed: A precertificate poison supplied through the pre-encoded Extension array was accepted without being critical, and RFC 6962 section 3.1 fixes it critical. A non-critical poison is ignored by a standard client, so the precertificate validated as an ordinary certificate rather than being refused, which is the single outcome the extension exists to prevent. Both pki.x509.sign and the pki.csr.sign extensionRequest now refuse it, alongside the nine certificate extensions whose criticality RFC 5280 section 4.2 fixes.
